label: Blood test

what_happens.title: What happens at a blood test
goals: The steps: sit down, sleeve up, band on the arm, clean wipe, quick pinch, a few drops in a tube, cotton and bandage
A tiny bit of blood helps the doctor learn how the body is doing
The body makes new blood all the time
what_happens.parentSkill: Name every step in order, including the pinch, and ask your child to say what comes next.

who_is_there.title: Who helps at the blood test
goals: A nurse or a phlebotomist takes the blood; their whole job is doing it gently
The grown-up stays close and holds the child
Other kids and grown-ups have blood tests too
who_is_there.parentSkill: Introduce the nurse by job, and plan where you will sit or hold your child.

what_i_do.title: What I do in the chair
goals: Sit on a lap or in a big chair and keep the arm floppy like a noodle
Look away or watch, it is my choice
Blow out slowly while the nurse works
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise the floppy noodle arm and the long slow blow-out together.

if_scared.title: If I feel scared
goals: A band squeezes tight, the wipe is cold, the pinch stings for a moment
It is okay to cry or say ouch; holding still is the brave part
Calm tools: blowing out, a comfort hug, a toy, looking at something fun
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling and stay honest: 'It may pinch for a moment. I'm right here holding you.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the blood test
goals: Play nurse with a toy: band, wipe, pretend pinch, bandage
Practise the noodle arm and the blow-out
Say the steps once more and end with the bandage and a treat
rehearsal.parentSkill: Let your child give a toy the pretend test first, then practise the comfort hold.

steps: Sit on a lap or in a big chair and roll up a sleeve
The nurse puts a stretchy band around the arm
A cold wipe cleans a small spot
A quick pinch, and a few drops of blood go into a tiny tube
Cotton and a press on the spot
Pick a bandage or a sticker
sensory: a stretchy band that squeezes the arm
a cold, wet wipe that smells clean
sometimes a finger prick that feels like a tiny poke
honestyNotes: A blood test usually pinches or stings for a moment. Say so plainly and never promise it will not be felt. Say the blood is a small amount and the body makes more. Do not describe needles in detail unless your child asks; follow the nurse about numbing cream.

fallbackAnswer: It may pinch or sting for a moment, like a quick poke.
Then it is over, and you can blow out slowly while it happens.

questionButtons.text: Why do they need my blood?
fallbackAnswer: A tiny bit of blood tells the doctor how your body is doing.
It is a way of checking, like a peek inside.

questionButtons.text: Will I have enough blood left?
fallbackAnswer: Yes. The nurse takes only a few drops, a tiny amount.
Your body makes new blood every day.
Yes. Crying is okay, and so is saying ouch.
Keeping your arm still is the brave part.
No. You can look away at a book or [[GROWNUP]]'s face, or you can watch.
Yes. [[GROWNUP]] can hold you in a big hug on a lap.
You are not alone for any part.
A nurse. Taking blood gently is their job, and they do it many times a day.
They will tell you each step before they do it.
After the blood test you get a bandage, and maybe a sticker.
Then we do something nice together.

techniques.label: A comfort hug on the lap
techniques.how: Sit your child on your lap, chest to chest or facing forward, and hug the free arm and legs gently.

techniques.label: Blowing out the birthday candles
techniques.how: Blow out slowly and long during the pinch, like many birthday candles, or blow bubbles.

techniques.label: A floppy noodle arm
techniques.how: Practise letting the arm go loose like a cooked noodle; a loose arm often feels less.

techniques.label: Looking at something fun
techniques.how: Bring a picture book or a video to look at during the test, or look into your eyes.

techniques.label: Asking about numbing cream
techniques.how: Ask the clinic ahead whether numbing cream or a cold spray is offered and follow their advice.

techniques.label: Choosing the bandage
techniques.how: Let your child choose the bandage or sticker beforehand so there is something to look forward to.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Bring a favourite toy that can sit on the lap and get a pretend test first.

techniques.label: Drinking water before
techniques.how: Offer water before the visit if the clinic allows it, and keep the arm warm with long sleeves.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: Sit on a lap and roll up a sleeve
Floppy arm and blow out slowly
Pick a bandage and do something nice

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will have a blood test.
A blood test means a nurse takes a tiny bit of blood, just a few drops.
The blood helps the doctor learn how [[CHILD]]'s body is doing.
First, [[CHILD]] sits on [[GROWNUP]]'s lap or in a big chair.
Then [[CHILD]] rolls up a sleeve.
Next, the nurse puts a stretchy band around the arm and cleans a spot with a cold wipe.
Then comes a quick pinch, and a few drops go into a tiny tube.
After that, a cotton ball and a press.
Last of all, [[CHILD]] picks a colourful bandage.
At the clinic there is a nurse.
Taking blood gently is the nurse's job.
The nurse does it many times a day, for big people and little people.
The nurse says hello and tells [[CHILD]] each step before it happens.
[[CHILD]] can say hello, or just wave.
[[GROWNUP]] stays right there the whole time.
[[CHILD]] can sit on [[GROWNUP]]'s lap for a big comfort hug.
A favourite toy can come too and sit close.
Lots of kids have blood tests, and so do lots of grown-ups.
[[CHILD]] can squeeze the toy when it is time.
In the chair, [[CHILD]] has two jobs.
The first job is a floppy noodle arm.
A floppy arm lets the nurse be quick, and it often feels like less of a pinch.
The second job is blowing out slowly, like a whole cake of birthday candles.
Whoosh, whoosh, and the pinch is over.
[[CHILD]] can choose where to look.
Some kids watch the nurse, and some kids look at a book or at [[GROWNUP]]'s face.
Both ways are fine.
Holding the arm still is the brave part, and the nurse is very careful.
[[CHILD]] can ask the nurse, what's next?
Some parts of a blood test feel strange.
The band on the arm squeezes tight.
The wipe feels cold and wet.
Then there is a quick pinch or a sting, and it can feel sore for a moment.
It is okay to feel scared about that, and it is okay to say ouch.
If [[CHILD]] cries, that is okay too.
Crying does not stop the brave part.
[[CHILD]] can hold [[GROWNUP]] tight, hug a toy, or blow out slowly.
Then the cotton and the bandage come, and the hard part is done.
[[GROWNUP]] gives [[CHILD]] a big proud hug.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] play nurse at home.
A hair tie can be the stretchy band, and a cotton ball can be the wipe.
First, [[CHILD]] gives a toy a pretend blood test.
Then it is [[CHILD]]'s turn.

First, sit and roll up a sleeve.
Then the band and the cold wipe.
Next, a quick pinch and blow out.
After that, the cotton and the bandage.
[[GROWNUP]] is proud of [[CHILD]] for practising, and gives a big hug.
